assignments.instructions_original:
What Should Be Included in Your Final Project Report?
Project Title and Team Members
What is your project title? Who are the members of your team?
Problem or Idea
What problem did you address, or what idea did you develop? Who are the intended users?
Project Objective
What did you aim to create, improve, or demonstrate?
Data / Information
What data or information did you use? Where did it come from, and how did you prepare it?
AI or Data Approach
How did you use AI or data? Describe the main tools, methods, and workflow.
Final Output and Results
What did you build or produce? Show how it works using examples, screenshots, or test results.
Potential Value
How could your solution help its intended users?
Limitations and Future Improvements
What did not work as expected? What would you improve or add next?
Team Contributions
What did each team member contribute? Briefly describe each person’s responsibilities and completed work.
References
List the sources, datasets, tools, and other materials used in your project.
Recommended Length
: 5–7 pages, including figures and tables, excluding the cover page and references.
Submission Format
: PDF. Submit code or other supporting materials as separate files or links.

assignments.assignment_title_original: Big Data Analytics and Modeling – Capstone Design Projects
assignments.assignment_title_english: Big Data Analytics and Modeling – Capstone Design Projects
assignments.instructions_original:
The
Capstone Design Project guidelines
for this semester are attached.
All students should carefully read the attached document and complete the Capstone Design activities
with their already assigned teams
.
The capstone consists of
two projects
:
Project 1 – End-to-End Predictive Analytics: From Raw Data to Model Comparison
Project 2 – Integrated Big Data Modeling: Robust Prediction, Interpretation, and Decision Support
These projects are designed to give you practical experience with the complete data analytics and modeling process, including data preparation, exploratory analysis, model development, model comparison, evaluation, interpretation, and communication of results.
Autumn_2026_Big_Data_Analytics_and_Modeling_Capstone_Design_Projects.docx
What You Need to Do
Work with your
already assigned team
throughout the Capstone Design activities.
Read the attached Capstone Design document carefully before beginning your project.
Follow the project requirements and complete each stage according to the
semester schedule provided in the document
.
Divide responsibilities appropriately among team members and maintain an organized record of your analysis and work.
Use
Python/Jupyter Notebook or Google Colab
for the analytical work. Students are expected to develop and understand their own analysis code.
Make sure your data preparation, modeling, evaluation, figures, tables, and conclusions are reproducible and can be explained by the team.
Complete the required reports, analysis files, and presentations at the specified project milestones.
Do not wait until the final submission week.
The projects must be developed progressively and reviewed at the scheduled checkpoints.
Important
The purpose of Capstone Design is
not simply to achieve the highest model accuracy
. Your team should be able to explain the complete analytical process, including why particular preprocessing methods, models, validation strategies, and evaluation metrics were selected.
Every team member should understand and be able to explain the team’s data, code, modeling process, results, limitations, and conclusions.
Generative AI and coding assistants may be used according to the guidelines provided in the attached document, but
AI-generated code or analysis must be understood, tested, and verified using the actual data
. Fabricated results, copied notebooks, or results that the team cannot explain are not acceptable.
Autumn_2026_Big_Data_Analytics_and_Modeling_Capstone_Design_Projects.docx
Please read the complete attached Capstone Design document carefully and follow the specified requirements and timeline throughout the semester.
